item.title: BROWN ALERT!
item.content:encoded:
Man you spooked me in a visceral way that few other skips have done. I noticed partway through that my hands were shaking and paused to take an anxiety pill. After I continued reading the bottle fell off my desk in this silent room and I damn near crapped myself.
This is an outstanding log and it'd be a crime if you don't continue with it. The only thing I can even find to complain about here is referring to the D-class as "they". He/she/it/whatever would be fine but using a pronoun as vague as "they" makes it feel to me like you're trying to hide some twist about the protagonist's identity that is never delivered.
But that's really just nitpicking, and you do deliver some great twists (or should I say crooks?) anyway. Both the corpses that grow and mutate when you're not looking to get in your face and the thing Singer became are such vivid images in my mind that I half expect to dream of this tonight.

Fucking bravo dude. I give it a +11 and will be sure to wear my brown pants when reading any future installments. This is right up there with the 093 logs for disturbing imagery.

item.content:encoded:
"They" is both singular and plural.
When a single person's gender is unknown (or pointedly irrelevant), they are referred to as "they".

Etymology bonus fact: Singular "they" predates plural "they" by at least a century of common usage. There are letters from "Ye Olden Days" bemoaning the then-current generations abuse of proper speech with the plural form.

item.content:encoded: Jesus christ this is fucking nightmare junji ito-tier shit, I know that gets thrown around alot but this is actually surreal and disgusting in a similar but still very distinct way. It's very clearly running on it's own insane internal logic that does not agree very well with human bodies, Both alive and dead. And the remains are not only disturbing to look at but it's clear it's also extremely painful for the people mutating into them. Though one thing I don't fully understand is why the explorer keeps being referred to as "they", I'm not the best with genderpolitics so that might have something to do with it. It's either that or the gender is being classified for some reason.
